name: Arousal Modulation
description: Neuromodulatory control of global brain state via noradrenaline, acetylcholine, and other transmitters. Regulates pupil dilation, heart rate, vigilance, and cortical excitability. Implemented by locus coeruleus (NE), basal forebrain (ACh), and other subcortical nuclei.
computational_signature: global_gain = f(arousal_level) where NE_level controls arousal
key_references: Aston-Jones, G., & Cohen, J. D. (2005). An integrative theory of locus coeruleus-norepinephrine function: Adaptive gain and optimal performance. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 28, 403-450.
Sara, S. J. (2009). The locus coeruleus and noradrenergic modulation of cognition. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 10(3), 211-223.
empirical_evidence: LC neurons fire together, releasing NE widely across cortex. Pupil diameter and NE levels correlate with task engagement. NE antagonists impair attention and learning. LC damage causes deficits in vigilance and arousal. ACh from basal forebrain controls cortical gain and learning state. Good evidence but causal mechanisms complex.
